author: Aaronjacobs000
summary: These parsers read two Datto RMM record types: monitor alerts and the Activity Log. Datto RMM Global Webhooks post the alerts straight to HTTP Ingest, and bridges/datto-rmm-activity-logs pulls the Activity Log from the API and posts each record to HTTP Ingest. Monitor alerts go to the third-party alert schema and Activity Log records go to CloudAudit.
notes:
Setup:
- Monitor alerts come from Datto RMM Global Webhooks, which can add an Authorization: Bearer header, posting the JSON payloads in README.md (Datto RMM payload variables) to a Sophos NG-SIEM HTTP Ingest integration.
- The Activity Log (logins, jobs, remote takeover and Web Remote sessions, file transfers, device and user changes) is only available from GET /v2/activity-logs, so bridges/datto-rmm-activity-logs pulls it and posts each record unchanged.

Field mapping:
- Monitor alerts go to the third-party alert schema.
- Activity Log records go to CloudAudit with the event name category.action.

Sources and licenses:
- Activity Log fields follow the ActivityLog schema in Datto's public API spec.

Made up in the samples:
- Datto doesn't list the categories and actions, so the samples use its example job.deployment and made-up ones for the rest, and the details text is kept as it is.
- Samples are made up in those formats.

Testing:
- Both parsers passed Run Test in a lab tenant on 2026-10-13: 104 of 104 fields matched the emulator, and the engine set the event time of the webhook alerts, which carry no time, to the ingest time.
- No built-in parser claimed these lines in 5 Run Tests.

Known gaps:
- The webhook parser assumes Datto escapes quotes and backslashes in payload values.
